question: What is the primary goal of instrument sterilization in primary health care settings?

options.A: To remove visible dirt and blood stains
options.B: To ensure instruments are completely free of all microbial life and spores
options.C: To reduce the microbial load on skin surfaces before surgery
options.D: To prolong the physical lifespan of surgical stainless steel

explanation: Sterilization aims to eliminate all forms of microbial life, including resistant bacterial spores, to prevent infections. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h1)

question: Why is proper instrument sterilization particularly critical for nurses in Nigerian primary health care facilities?

options.A: It helps prevent healthcare-associated infections and blood-borne pathogen transmission during procedures
options.B: It is only required for major teaching hospitals and tertiary centers
options.C: It eliminates the need for any hand hygiene practices
options.D: It guarantees that instruments never require sharpening or maintenance

explanation: Nurses must prevent infections and blood-borne pathogen transmission during common PHC procedures like wound dressings and deliveries. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h1)

question: What is the primary purpose of the decontamination step using a 0.5% chlorine solution?

options.A: To completely sterilize the instruments within five minutes
options.B: To remove bio-burden and protect staff from infectious splashes
options.C: To polish the stainless steel surface
options.D: To dry the instruments before packaging

explanation: Decontamination neutralizes body fluids and protects personnel from infections while handling contaminated items. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h2)

question: Why is physical cleaning considered an absolute prerequisite before sterilization?

options.A: Organic matter can shield microorganisms and prevent sterilizing agents from working effectively
options.B: It makes the instruments look brand new
options.C: It eliminates the need to use an autoclave
options.D: It prevents the instruments from getting wet

explanation: Remaining organic debris acts as a barrier that blocks heat or chemical sterilants from reaching underlying microbes. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h2)

question: Which physical sterilization method is considered the gold standard for most heat-stable medical instruments?
explanation: Steam sterilization under pressure is highly reliable, penetrates well, and rapidly destroys all forms of microbial life. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h3)

question: When would a nurse choose a chemical sterilization method instead of steam autoclaving?

options.A: When sterilizing heavy surgical forceps and stainless steel basins
options.B: When dealing with heat-sensitive items like delicate endoscopes
options.C: When electricity and water are completely unavailable
options.D: When trying to reduce the total processing time to under one minute

explanation: Chemical agents are chosen for heat-sensitive instruments that would be damaged by the high temperatures of steam or dry heat. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h3)

question: What are the standard operating parameters for a typical gravity displacement steam autoclave?
explanation: Standard autoclave cycles commonly utilize 121°C at 15 psi for 15 to 30 minutes to ensure complete spore destruction. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h4)

question: How should instrument packs be arranged inside the autoclave chamber to ensure effectiveness?

options.A: Stacked tightly in a flat, horizontal pile to save space
options.B: Arranged loosely on their edges to allow free steam circulation
options.C: Wrapped tightly in thick plastic bags to keep them dry
options.D: Placed directly on the heating elements at the bottom

explanation: Loose arrangement on edges ensures that steam can circulate freely and penetrate every single instrument pack. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h4)

question: What is a major advantage of dry heat sterilization over steam autoclaving?

options.A: It works in half the time of an autoclave
options.B: It does not cause rusting on sharp metal instruments
options.C: It can safely sterilize rubber gloves and plastic tubing
options.D: It requires zero electricity or fuel

explanation: Dry heat lacks moisture, making it safe for sharp cutting instruments that would otherwise rust in steam. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h5)

question: Why is boiling water considered a disinfection method rather than true sterilization?

options.B: It does not reliably destroy highly resistant bacterial spores
options.C: It damages stainless steel within seconds

explanation: While boiling kills vegetative organisms, bacterial spores can survive 100°C, meaning boiling does not achieve true sterilization. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h5)

question: What type of indicator is considered the gold standard for confirming that a sterilization cycle was successful?

options.C: Biological indicators containing resistant bacterial spores

explanation: Biological indicators use actual resistant spores to test whether the sterilizer successfully destroys all microbial life. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h6)

question: What is the primary limitation of chemical indicator strips placed inside instrument packs?

options.B: They change color even if no instruments are inside the chamber
options.C: They confirm exposure to specific conditions but do not definitively prove sterility
options.D: They dissolve completely when exposed to steam

explanation: Chemical indicators show that exposure parameters were met, but only biological indicators test actual microbial destruction. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h6)

question: What does 'event-related sterility' mean for stored sterile instrument packages?

options.A: Packs expire automatically after exactly seven days
options.B: Packs remain sterile unless the packaging is compromised, torn, or wet
options.C: Sterility depends entirely on the ambient room temperature
options.D: Instruments lose their sterility every time a nurse touches them

explanation: Sterility is maintained until an event occurs, such as a tear or moisture exposure, that compromises the packaging barrier. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h7)

question: Why must newly sterilized packs be allowed to cool completely before being handled or stored?

options.A: To prevent the metal instruments from melting the storage shelves
options.B: To prevent condensation from drawing microorganisms through the wrapper via wicking
options.C: To ensure the chemical indicator changes back to its original color
options.D: To speed up the drying process of the autoclave chamber

explanation: Handling warm packs creates condensation that can cause wicking, pulling bacteria through damp packaging material. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of maintaining a unidirectional workflow in a sterile processing department?

options.A: To reduce electricity consumption in the clinic
options.B: To prevent cross-contamination by separating dirty cleaning areas from sterile storage areas
options.C: To allow nurses to finish their shifts much faster
options.D: To keep the autoclave machine running at maximum pressure

explanation: A unidirectional workflow ensures that contaminated items never cross paths with clean or sterilized equipment, preventing cross-contamination. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h8)

question: Which measure is recognized as the single most effective way to prevent the spread of infections in healthcare settings?

options.A: Wearing heavy-duty rubber aprons at all times
options.C: Using chemical sprays on all clinic furniture hourly

explanation: Hand hygiene is universally acknowledged as the most effective baseline measure to interrupt the transmission of infectious agents. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h8)
